title: Ambiguous canary targeting caused routing lockout and capacity skew — recovery & hardening plan
creator: Diego Alvarez
description: Summary: During a targeted model rollout on runtime-2.3.0, overlapping canary targeting rules combined with weight rounding produced a deterministic route lockout. A small autoscaling hiccup then concentrated traffic against a pinned default variant, producing sustained elevated latency and a 6% error rate for affected customers. This ticket tracks follow-ups, fixes, and hardening to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-03-11 02:03 UTC — Alert: latency SLO breach for /generate route; on-call notified (pager).
2026-03-11 02:07 UTC — Initial triage: increased 5xxs and latency correlated with a model rollout for tenant cohort A; canary weight reported at 12% but traffic showed 40% to default variant.

2026-03-11 02:20 UTC — Mitigation: ops pinned route to runtime-2.2.9 and temporarily disabled canary targeting for cohort selectors matching header X-Cohort-A; latency recovered to baseline by 02:40 UTC.
2026-03-11 08:00 UTC — Post-incident analysis started; constructed query of router logs, metrics, and canary state snapshots.
2026-03-12 11:00 UTC — Root cause hypothesis validated: ambiguous predicate ordering + weight rounding + greedy matching semantics in route translator produced unexpected traffic routing.
root_cause: Three contributing faults: (1) Canary targeting rules used partially-overlapping predicates (header AND path variants) which the route translator evaluated with last-wins precedence; (2) Canary weight stored as a 16-bit scaled int and subject to rounding which pushed a 12% configured weight to an effective 37% on a particular distribution of hash values; (3) Autoscaler transiently reduced available dedicated capacity during a spike, so fallback/default variant received more of the shifted traffic and experienced headroom exhaustion leading to 5xxs and latency. The combination produced a persistent routing lockout where the translator favored the default route despite configuration intent.
mitigation: Hotfix deployed 2026-03-11 04:15 UTC: route-translator guarded against overlapping predicate ambiguity by rejecting overlapping canary rules during apply and returning clear diagnostics to console.
Pinned rollout to previous stable model for impacted tenants until hardening is validated (action completed).
Manual capacity bump for Dedicated pools serving cohort A for the rest of the day to reduce pressure on fallback variants.
action_items: ENG-51774: Add static assertion in rollout config validator to detect overlapping predicates and fail fast with human-readable errors (owner: S. Kim, estimate: 3).
ENG-51775: Replace 16-bit scaled weight with higher-precision representation and add unit tests for pathological hash distributions (owner: R. Singh, estimate: 5).
ENG-51776: Improve router diagnostics: expose effective routing weights and per-route hit histograms to Console within 30s (owner: L. Zhao, estimate: 8).
ENG-51777: Autoscaler postmortem and throttle smoothing: add transient-surge guard to avoid capacity dips during rollouts (owner: M. Thompson, estimate: 5).
ENG-51778: Runbook update: include immediate checklist for canary misrouting (rollback, pin, capacity bump, communicate) and schedule tabletop exercise (owner: A. Patel, estimate: 2).
ENG-51779: Add alert rule for effective-route-weight drift (>x% from configured) with playbook link (owner: SRE team, estimate: 2).

2026-03-13 09:11 — Diego: Confirmed unit test coverage reproduces rounding edge-case locally. PR 6612 opened with weight representation change.

resolution: Short-term: pinned impacted tenants to previous model and deployed route-translator reject-on-overlap hotfix. Medium-term: weight precision change and router diagnostics scheduled. Long-term: rollout configuration migration tool and autoscaler smoothing. Tracking implementation across ENG-51774..ENG-51779; target complete before next major rollout window (2026-04-05).
